title: CPSC says a water heater at 120 degrees Fahrenheit or lower lowers scald risk in the bath
summary: CPSC says to stay within reach at bath time because a child can drown quickly, and that the water heater can be set to 120 degrees Fahrenheit or lower.
body: In the bath section, CPSC says to give constant supervision and stay within reach when a baby is bathing, because children can drown in moments. To prevent burns, it says the water heater can be set to 120 degrees Fahrenheit or lower. Anti-scald devices on faucets and shower heads are another option it names. UNICEF's parenting page, a different voice, talks about a child's thinner skin and a bath near body temperature. This card is only the US heater figure and the paired warning to stay within reach. It is not a treatment for a burn. Burn first aid is on the first-aid burn card.
